newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Controversial Colombian envoy to EU resigns.
newsitem.headline: Controversial Colombian envoy to EU resigns.

text.p: Colombia's controversial envoy to the European Union, a diplomat linked in recent news reports to right-wing paramilitary activity, has tendered his resignation, authorities said on Wednesday.

Ambassador Carlos Arturo Marulanda, who has served in the Brussels-based post for the past 5-1/2 years, announced his intention to step down in a letter on Tuesday to President Ernesto Samper, the text of which was made public by the foreign ministry.
It was not immediately clear how soon he would actually abandon the mission or who his replacement would be.

Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia told reporters last month that growing pressure from some European countries and human rights groups for Marulanda's removal as ambassador to the EU was a cause of "enormous concern" to Bogota.
She did not elaborate, but diplomatic sources said Samper had been pressing for Marulanda's resignation since he took office in August 1994.

Recent editorial commentaries, and a lengthy expose in Bogota's El Espectador newspaper, have linked Marulanda and his brother to paramilitary activity, political killings and the eviction of landless peasants from their family's sprawling estate in northern Cesar province.
Marulanda, who was appointed ambassador the EU by former president Cesar Gaviria, denied any wrongdoing in his letter to Samper.
